records.title: S2:E4 - Tom's Disclosure Day: Can he actually bend spoons with his mind?
records.description:
“I feel awkward saying this.”


That’s how it opens. Asim had been badgering Tom to record this since February and Tom had been finding reasons not to.


What happened was that Tom sat holding a spoon, thumb resting on it with almost no pressure, eyes closed, picturing a bend, and meditated to find love in his heart and an intense desire for the spoon to bend. He didn’t expect anything to happen. And then:


“It just suddenly moved in my hand and folded over. And I just freaked out.”


The panic came first. The excitement arrived a beat behind it.


“Holy s**t, what just happened? I did it.”


That’s where this episode begins, and it is the gateway to insights that you might not expect.


Why the resistance?


Asim believed Tom instantly all the way back in February, but Tom wasn’t comfortable talking about it publicly. He had direct experience of something inexplicable happening and had multiple pieces of physical evidence to prove it, yet still resisted it even within himself.


That’s the discovery of the episode, that modern humans seem to have an inability to process things that present too much of a challenge to their model of the world. Our own minds try to rewrite the past to make it fit into the old paradigm, and then social pressures reinforce those limits. We stay inside the lines and move on with our lives as if nothing happened.


It isn’t hidden. There’s a booking link.


The standard argument against strange phenomena is often availability: if it’s real, why isn’t everyone doing it?


But this isn’t even hidden. The Monroe Institute runs a spoon-bending workshop. It’s four hours, on Zoom. It isn’t hidden in a cave in Tibet or inside a secret society. It’s here in plain sight, and yet we pretend we haven’t seen it. Which means the suppression isn’t happening out there, but inside of ourselves.


Tom thinks that’s what most anomalies do. Plenty of people have had an experience that doesn’t fit, and rather than let it detonate their worldview, they discount it and move on. Asim actually has a tattoo specifically to stop himself doing this — somewhere he can’t avoid looking, because otherwise the strangest thing that ever happened to him would fade into the background like a dream.


Spoons are the door


Halfway through, Asim says he’s nervous about moving on from spoons, because moving on is exactly the shelving behaviour we had just diagnosed. So we stay, and it opens out.


If your mind can alter steel, then consciousness and matter aren’t the separate categories we’ve been told. Telekinesis becomes a kind of manifestation; manifestation becomes a claim about consciousness; and with that, telepathy and remote viewing become almost trivial.


“Historically, in my mind, these have all been separate things. But they’re actually all just the same thing.”


Which raises the possibility that we don’t manifest things within the rules of reality, we manifest the rules. Tom’s route there is the observer — every experiment ever run needed someone to look and write it down, so consciousness isn’t a topic within physics, it’s the precondition. Once you notice that, permanent laws start to look less fundamental.


The closest thing we could find to a physical explanation for spoons actually bending came from Dean Radin at the Institute of Noetic Science, but it covers about half of it and leaves the important half untouched. Tom’s fine with that:


“There’s a point at which people should stop clutching at straws and just say: we don’t know.”


The film about aliens that isn’t about aliens


Tom’s spoon bending wasn’t the only disclosure in the episode. We went to see Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day together at the IMAX. Tom enjoyed it while Asim spent two hours interrogating its motives. Spoilers ahead.


Tom’s catch is to ask, where is your attention while watching that film? On the aliens, on whether they’ll be revealed — that’s the whole basis of the plot. And yet you barely see one. What you actually watch, scene after scene, is telepathy, telekinesis, remote viewing, being acted out in plain sight while the script writers keep your eyes on the skies. Magicians call that misdirection.


There are breadcrumbs in the film too, if you like breadcrumbs — a military character with always exactly the same name as a real general who signed the 1947 memo saying the UFO phenomenon was real and not visionary or fictitious, and a defector called Hugo Wakefield, whose name means something approximating to “watch your mind”. Tom doesn’t claim to know what it means. He just doesn’t think the film is about aliens.


So who is disclosing what?


Asim’s objection isn’t to the pattern, it’s to the motive. Aliens he can model: if it’s real and uncontrollable you control the narrative instead, and if it’s advanced hardware the alien story is superb cover. But telepathy and telekinesis don’t compute — psychic ability is the last capability an intelligence apparatus would want distributed.

🛠️ Hacking the Circuit

records.title: MA v Lindsay Clancy - Dr Gregory Saathoff - FBI Forensic Psychiatrist - Behavioral Analysis Unit
records.description:
Testimony of Dr. Gregory Saathoff in the Lindsay Clancy trial regarding bipolar II, command hallucinations, and criminal responsibility:

_Witness Background & Qualifications_
•   *Education:* Undergraduate degree at University of Notre Dame. M.D. at University of Missouri. Psychiatry residency at University of Virginia.
•   *Appointments:* Professor of emergency medicine and public health sciences at University of Virginia. Senior psychiatrist for FBI Behavioral Analysis Unit (BAU) at Quantico since 1996. Consulting psychiatrist for Virginia Department of Corrections state prison facilities.
•   *Board Certification:* Absence of board certification in forensic psychiatry due to military and public psychiatry commitments preventing a one-year fellowship.
•   *Testimony:* Previous court testimony as a forensic psychiatrist approximately 40 to 45 times.

_Evaluation Scope_
•   *Retention:* Retained by Plymouth County District Attorney's Office with compensation remitted directly to the University of Virginia.
•   *Interviews:* Two remote Zoom interviews with Lindsay Clancy totaling ~11.5 hours (May 29, 2026 for 6.5 hours. June 4, 2026 for 5 hours). Remote Zoom collateral interview with Patrick Clancy.

_Direct Examination Opinions_
•   *Reported Hallucinations:* Reported male command voice ("This is your last chance...") allegedly starting at 534 PM after a phone call with her husband and ending immediately after strangling youngest child Callan.
•   *Atypical Features:* First-ever reported auditory hallucination, continuous tape-like repetition, abrupt stopping upon child's death, and absence of accompanying delusions. Marked timeline inconsistency between account given to Dr. Saathoff (onset at 534 PM) and account given to Dr. Spinelli (onset at 510–515 PM upon husband's departure).
•   *Planning:* Calculated errand arrangement (online distance searches for ThreeV restaurant and CVS prior to texting husband) to ensure prolonged absence. Methodical strangulations using basement exercise bands without explicit instructions from the reported voice regarding method, sequence, or location.
•   *Diagnosis:* Formal diagnosis of Bipolar II disorder linked to SSRI-induced (Zoloft) severe insomnia. Resolution of intrusive thoughts with Ativan (lorazepam), indicating non-psychotic intrusive anxiety rather than true command hallucinations.
•   *Criminal Responsibility:* Opinion to reasonable medical certainty: capacity to appreciate right from wrong and ability to conform behavior to law. Full criminal responsibility on January 24, 2023.

_Cross-Examination (Attorney Reddington)_
•   *Evaluation Conditions:* Evaluation conducted via Zoom three years post-incident. Primary clinical focus in prison/government settings rather than traditional private outpatient care. Extensive published research focused heavily on national security, terrorism, threat assessment, and female extremism rather than postpartum depression.
•   *Testing & Research:* Lack of published articles on auditory hallucinations. Reference to Dr. Phillip Resnick's 2014 study. Omission of laboratory testing (blood drug levels, enzyme metabolizing tests, thyroid screens prior to ER visit). Results of MMPI testing (administered by Dr. Heilbrun) showing truthfulness and no indicia of malingering.

_Redirect (Attorney Sprague)_
•   *Guidelines:* World Health Organization diagnostic guidelines for postpartum onset within six weeks of delivery. Normal thyroid levels documented at South Shore ER in November 2022.
•   *Treatment:* Standard low-dose titration protocol (25 mg) for Lamictal prescribing to minimize rash risk. Failure of defendant to inform treating clinicians of decision not to take Lamictal. Responsive outpatient care by Dr. Tufts (14 video visits). Aspire suicide hotline protocol: referral to day programs after defendant explicitly denied an active suicide plan.

Brown also introduces his comparative research on phenomenological differences between mindfulness meditation, self-hypnosis, and waking dreaming, exploring how distinct awareness disciplines produce measurably different inner states across attention, emotion, body sensation, time sense, and sense of self.

A foundational talk at the intersection of contemplative tradition and empirical psychology.

---

 Topics covered:
- Anxiety and emotion regulation in long-term meditators
- Rorschach findings and personality structure
- Comparative phenomenology: meditation vs. hypnosis vs. imaging
- Stages of mindfulness — cross-cultural validation
- Implications for psychotherapy and Western psychology

---
 Research Findings (from the lecture)

Brown's team collected before/after data from students on three-month retreats at IMS using psychological tests, Rorschach assessments, teacher evaluations, and a purpose-built meditation questionnaire. Key results:

- **Anxiety:** Initial increase in reported anxiety during the first week or two of intensive practice, followed by a significant drop — ending well below pre-retreat baseline. Effects persisted at one-year follow-up.
- **Emotional life:** Practitioners reported a broader range of emotions, experienced with greater intensity, yet observed with less reactivity — more in touch with feelings, but less destabilized by them.
- **Body awareness:** Universally increased across all participants regardless of personality type or presenting issues — with corresponding reductions in psychosomatic complaints.
- **Personality structure:** Core personality did not change, but the *relationship* to it shifted dramatically — practitioners developed a new perspective on their own character rather than altered traits.
- **Attention:** Only ~50% of three-month retreat students maintained single-object concentration throughout; questionnaire data mapped attentional styles to practice stages.
- **Rorschach:** Different meditation styles produced measurably different perceptual styles — suggesting practice-specific effects rather than a generic "relaxation response."
- **Stages validation:** Questionnaire responses correlated with teacher assessments of where students were in their practice, empirically supporting a stage model of meditation development.

And why does thinking more sometimes make us feel less certain?

We often assume that overthinking means we're thinking deeply.

But there's an important difference.

Deep thinking moves you toward an answer.
Overthinking keeps asking the same question without moving forward.

I talked with Jonathan Ashford, not as an interview, but as a real back-and-forth, a former executive who died for three hours after a missed medical diagnosis and came back a different person, all at once, not over years of practice. We talk about what he was shown about unconditional love, what it was like for him to come back without the usual work of integration, and why he doesn't see his old life as a mistake. By Ulrike Granögger

When I went to the 2024 Water Conference (which turned out to be the last Water Conference in a magnificent series of events since 2006) to present on the Wave Genome, one of the most memorable speakers was Githa Ben-David from Denmark. She came with her co-worker Merete Vestergaard and the Israeli filmmaker Tsipi Raz and spoke about the unique healing power of your own voice. At the end of her presentation, she showed a short clip from an upcoming documentary that blew everybody’s mind. The footage (part of which is also included in this Solari interview) shows a medical miracle where a tumor recedes in a matter of minutes in what appears to be a response to the mere influence of vocal sound. What an extraordinary intuition and scientific daring for conference organizer Professor Gerald Pollack to invite her as a speaker.

Githa and I have since become friends, and I am inspired to introduce her work to the Solari community as a prime instrument of self-help and liberation on several levels all at once. For the Note from Heaven is not first and foremost about “healing” (and to be clear: nothing in this interview should be regarded as medical advice, its content is meant to serve educational purposes only) but about “knowing thyself”! It is about finding your own frequency and accessing your own authenticity—and that can ultimately lead to opening the body’s ability to heal itself.

Githa discovered that which she calls the Note from Heaven when she learned classical raga singing in Varanasi, India, as taught by the late Mangala Tiwari, a highly esteemed classical Indian singer from the “House of Benares” and representative of the Khyal style of vocalization. Tiwari instructed Githa to sing one note for an hour, an exercise that provoked resistance at first. “Why sing just one note?” A while into the exercise, however, the note changed, the voice became rich with overtones that echoed from all sides despite singing alone—the note from heaven had arrived!

Githa writes in The Ultimate Book on Vocal Sound Healing (p. 5):

    “The Note from Heaven is the tonal expression of a divine state that we all have within us and we can all contact. When you experience the Note from Heaven, the note seems to sing you, rather than you singing it.”

The Note from Heaven is your own characteristic frequency. Don’t expect it to be a specific number of cycles per second (Hz). That would be simplistic. Rather, it is that which sings inside of you, continually singing “yes” to life and “yes” to yourself. Githa writes (p. 454):

    “We are each born with our own fundamental frequency. It doesn’t pay to try to change your fundamental frequency in order to adapt to your surroundings. Your fundamental frequency is you. If you run away from it, you lose yourself. The prerequisite for meeting true resonance in another person is that you completely uphold your own sound.”

When have you last listened to your own voice? Consciously, and with interest? In a world that is numbed by an ever-increasing “shriek-o-meter” and scrambled with constant distortive and manipulative EMFs, getting in touch with your own voice is the simplest and most direct way to clarity and self-knowledge. From this perspective, Githa says (p. 5), “The Note from Heaven is not in itself the goal. Its function is to free the voice, and through that to expand consciousness.”

In her discovery of the Note from Heaven, Githa realized that there are many more features of the inherent power of our own voices, and this journey has brought forth new tools of well-being, healing, and self-realization. Not only overtones, but also undertones (subharmonics) can be utilized to access parts of the body and the anatomy of the soul. In this interview, I have tried to touch upon all these elements with the intention of stimulating your own search for your authentic voice of inner freedom and the magic of song. Voice and sound are primeval powers.

Solari’s in-house cinematographer Robert Dupper filmed this interview in the beautiful surroundings of a three-day workshop that we had just concluded with Githa and Merete. A testimony of one of the participants is included at the end. We hope you enjoy this production. Check out Githa’s work and follow your own note toward wholeness and freedom.
